justification.description: Why the company needs it: shown on the hire approval.

org_role.description: Absent: none (`ceo` and `cto` at most once per company).

failed_over_to.description: The attempt that replaced this one.

An ordered fallback chain of 1 to 4 pools. A new session draws an account from the first
entry that has one to give.

One step of a chain: the pool tried at this position, and the harness and model its accounts
run. The harness is the pool's provider's own.

Pin the entry to one account of the company's pool; absent: any. (No account is in a
pool until the accounts slice, so a pin is refused for now.)

The chain agents with no chain of their own use.

challenge.description:
32 bytes, base64url (43 characters), opaque to the client; spend it once within
`expires_in` seconds.

A passkey device's step-up only: `{"publicKey": PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions}`
over `challenge`, for `navigator.credentials.get`.

device_id.description: The device that will answer it, `d_…`.

ClaimBody.description:
A claim. The credential hash is SHA-256 of the canonical typed code (upper-cased, dashes
and spaces dropped, `I`/`L` read as `1` and `O` as `0`: 10 ASCII Crockford characters), or
of the QR secret's 16 decoded bytes (not its base64 text). Vectors:
`crates/server/tests/vectors/pairing-v1.json`.

code.description: The typed code (`ABCDE-FGHJK`, any case); or `secret`.

device_name.description:
What to call this device: 1 to 64 characters of plain text, no control characters. It
becomes the device's name in place of the pairing's (an invite's is `owner`).

pop.description:
The routine key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-PAIR-V1` LF `<core_fp>` LF `<base64url of the credential hash>` LF
`<fp(routine)>` LF `<fp(stepup) or ->`, no trailing newline; fp is base64url SHA-256 of
the SPKI.

pop_stepup.description: The step-up key over the same string, with `stepup_spki`.

routine_spki.description: The routine key: a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64url.

stepup_spki.description: The step-up key, where the device has one.

core_spki.description: The Core identity SPKI, base64url: its fingerprint must equal the QR's `c`.

device_id.description: The new device, `d_…`, pending until approved; for an invite it is active already.

pairing_id.description:
The pairing, `p_…`: with `core_spki` and its own key the device computes the SAS
itself and shows that, rather than trusting `sas` from whoever answered.

sas.description:
Show this; the approver compares it with theirs. The first 16 upper-case Crockford
characters of SHA-256(`AINKRAD-SAS-V1` ‖ core_spki ‖ routine_spki ‖ pairing id as
UTF-8), as `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`. Meaningless for an invite: nothing waits on a match.

anyOf.description: How hard an agent thinks (API minor 17).

elevated_until.description: Until when this session may call routes marked `x-ainkrad-destructive`.

url.description: Empty when it has none; never holding credentials.

epic_id.description: Absent takes it out of its epic.

EpicPatchBody.description:
An epic's fields to change (API minor 18); absent fields keep their value, `null` clears an
optional one.

requirement_id.description: One of the project company's requirements.

ErrorBody.description: A JSON error: a stable `code` and a message for people.

error_id.description:
`err_` and a ULID, unique to this answer: logged with it (and, for a refused write,
audited as `api.refused`), for the app's "Copy error".

server_time.description: The server's clock in unix seconds, on a `clock_skew` refusal only (handshake spec §5.3).

points.description: Story points; absent clears the estimate.

Event.description:
One entry of the event stream. `seq` only grows: it is the replay cursor, counted gap-free over
the events this device's scopes may see (`x-event-scopes`), so it differs between devices
with different scopes. New kinds may be added: a client skips an event whose kind it does not
know.

kind.description:
What happened: `audit` (an audited change; the payload is the audit row: `audit_seq`,
`action`, `actor_kind`, `actor_id`, `entity_kind`, `entity_id`, `entity_ref`, `details`;
a device is named by its `d_…` id in `entity_ref`, with `entity_id` null), or a kind a
module writes. The registered kinds are listed in `x-event-kinds`. The payload of
`agent.state` is `{session, state, reason, …}`: a live session that finished its answer is
`state: "waiting"` with `reason: "turn_ended"` (its transcript has the harness's
`turn_ended` and a `waiting` entry), and `state: "running"` with `reason: "message"` when
the next message starts an answer. A chain session that waits for an account
says `reason: "waiting"` and `waiting: {until, why, since}` (`until` an RFC 3339 time, `since`
the first wait in unix seconds), and one whose launch refused its account, so another was
picked across a provider or harness, says `reason: "repicked"`, and a run a failover moved across
them says `reason: "failover"`, both with `from` and `to` (each `{provider, harness}`). `account.limited` is `{account, class, until, source}`: an account
cooled or limited until `until` (`class` `rate_limited`, `quota` or `plan_limit`; `source`
`gateway` or `harness`). `account.health` is `{account, user, state, reason}`: an account went
`unhealthy` (`reason` `upstream_errors` or `auth_suspected`). `account.failover` is `{run,
user, from_session, to_session, from_account, to_account, from_pool, to_pool, class, hop}`: a
run moved to `to_session`, or ended (`to_session` null: its chain has nothing left, the hop cap
or the storm guard; `to_account` is null while the successor waits for one). `account.budget` is
`{subject_kind, subject, state}` for an account's or a pool's budget (`state` `warning` or
`exhausted`). `account.expired` is `{account, user, reason}`: a key the provider refused was
confirmed and the account disabled. `alarm.raised` with `alarm` `failover_storm` and a
`user` says the bound on that user's failovers stopped a run of theirs from moving (once per
window and user). `connection.health` is `{connection, user, kind, state, reason}`: a connection's
health changed (`state` `active`, `cooling`, `limited`, `unhealthy` or `disabled`; `reason` a fixed
code: `rate_limited`, `quota`, `upstream_errors`, `auth_suspected`, `auth_failed`, `recovered`,
`auth_cleared`). It is visible to `admin` devices only (`x-event-scopes`), never to a `read` device;
the push for it goes to the owning user's admin devices only. No payload holds a key, a token or an
upstream's own words.

EventActor.description: Who acted, on an audited change.

anyOf.description:
What an agent's figure shows, first match wins:

| state | when |
|---|---|
| `sleepy` | the agent is paused |
| `rest` | it waits on its hire approval, or is terminated |
| `listening` | it has an open question to the admin, or an approval it asked for is pending |
| `working` | its run is running and has produced output |
| `thinking` | its run is running, no output yet |
| `loading` | its run is queued or claimed by a runner, not yet started |
| `confused` | its last run failed, timed out, lost its runner or stalled |
| `success` | its last run succeeded in the last five minutes |
| `idle` | otherwise |

Until the run engine is ported only the first three and `idle` occur.

Handshake.description: What the server is and speaks, for anyone.

api_minor.description: The contract minor this server speaks (`GET /api/v1/me` has it too).

git_sha.description: The commit it was built from (short sha), when the build knew it.

identity_fingerprint.description:
`core_fp`: base64url SHA-256 of the Core identity key's SPKI, 43 characters. Signed
into every request (handshake spec §5.2).

supported_minors.description:
Every minor a client may have been built against and still be served: 0 up to
`api_minor`.

HandshakeBody.description: A liveness proof request: a fresh nonce from the client.

nonce.description: 16 random bytes, base64url without padding (22 characters).

HandshakeProof.description:
`POST /handshake`'s answer: `GET`'s fields plus the proof, which is always present (review
L4). A client that pinned `core_fp` aborts with `core_identity_mismatch` when either is
missing or fails, and never falls back to `GET /handshake` (spec §13).

core_sig.description:
The Core identity key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-CORE-V1` LF `<host>` LF `<nonce>`, no trailing newline; `host` is the Core's
configured Host (the `Host` it requires), `nonce` the text the client sent.

core_spki.description:
The Core identity key, a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64url. Its fingerprint is
`identity_fingerprint`.

identity_fingerprint.description: `core_fp`, as in `GET /handshake`; a client checks `fp(core_spki)`, not this claim.

criteria.description: The acceptance criteria, in order (API minor 18).

advanced.description: Shown under "Advanced", not as the first choice.

available.description:

help.description: A plain sentence for the screen.

steps.description: The steps the screen shows, in order.

KindLimit.description: A key of the resource limit a grant may carry.

body_truncated.description: The body was cut to 16 KiB in a list.

proposed_by_agent_id.description: The agent that proposed it; absent for an entry the admin added.

rationale.description: The proposer's one-line reason for it.

reason.description: Why it was accepted or rejected.

status.description: `retired`: kept for history, never given to a run.

superseded_by.description: The entry that replaced this one.

target.description: What accepting a proposal applies its body to: `spec` or `profile.<field>`.

Label.description: A label of a project, put on its issues.

name.description: One line, 1–50 characters, unique in the project.

LastTest.description: The last one-shot test of an account's key.

result.description:
The status class the provider answered: `ok`, `rate_limited`, `quota`, `auth_failed`,

LatestEvent.description: The newest event's seq a client would be shown: the catch-up target.

floor.description:
The retention floor: events up to it were trimmed, so a client whose last read seq is
below it re-syncs (E1-04.4). Absent from servers before API minor 2.

LeaseGrant.description:
A granted lease: hand `lease` to the runner, which redeems it once before `expires_at`.

lease.description: `l_…`; only its runner can redeem it.

expires_at.description: Drop it by then, or at the session's end.

kind.description:
`text`, `multiline`, `file` (the value is base64: decode it, write it as `file_name`

LimitStanding.description: A limit and how much of it is used.

secret_name.description: The broker secret holding the API token, `citadel.linear.<name>`.

Lockout.description: A key that is locked now.

strikes.description: Locks in a row; each doubles the next.

LogLine.description: A page of a service's log, redacted by the helper, newest entries at the end.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next older page; absent on the last.

LoginCode.description: The approval code the user pasted. No `Debug`: it is a one-time secret.

code.description: 8 to 512 of letters, digits and `-_.~#:+/=`; passed to the runner and dropped.

Me.description: The calling device and what the server speaks.

capacity.description: Points it takes on per sprint; absent when not set.

ModelFallback.description: One entry of the fallback chain, tried in order after the agent's own harness and model.

input_per_mtok_micro.description: List price per million input tokens, in millionths of a dollar.

ModelTier.description:
The (harness, model) an agent's tasks of `tier` start on. Its own harness and model are
its standard tier, so only `small` and `large` are set here.

anchor_issue_id.description: The issue to go before or after.

anyOf.description: Where an issue goes in its project's order.

Named.description: A device: who, by id and name.

NewAgentSession.description: A session to start. No `Debug`: the prompt is the caller's.

agent.description:
An opaque agent id (1 to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`): its bound chain, else the user's
default chain, serves the session. Needs `admin`. With no chain either way the session
runs as a plain one and names its harness.

chain.description:
A fallback chain's id: the session draws its account from it, one at a time. Needs
`admin`. It must not come with a harness, a model or an `acct.*` secret.

connection_access.description:
Capability names the session may call through its connections (`read_repo`,
`issues_write`, `read_issues`, ...; see `listConnectionKinds`). Needs `admin`. Absent: the
default, read-class capabilities only (write is an explicit grant); an agent's session
with none has no connection tools. An empty list is refused (400 `empty_allowlist`), and
so are operation names and `*` (400).

harness.description:
`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `agy` (what the runner's `agent` driver takes). Omit it
(and `model`) when the session draws from a chain: the account the allocator picks sets them.

live.description:
One live conversation (default `true`): the harness stays up after each answer, the state
is `waiting` until the next `sendAgentMessage`, and the session ends only on `cancel`,
`kill`, the idle end (`agents.idle_end_secs`) or when the CLI exits by itself. `false`, or
a runner that does not offer it (the answer's `live` says), runs one answer and ends.

model.description:
The model id as the provider names it. For a session served by the auth gateway it must be
one of the ids priced for its provider, exactly: the gateway resolves no alias.

prompt.description:
The first message. Absent or empty: the session starts with no message, like opening the
CLI: its harness is up, the state is `waiting`, and the first message comes through
`sendAgentMessage`. A message gives the session its `title` (its first 60 characters).

secrets.description: At most 16. Each is leased to the runner at each start (secrets broker, gate G-SEC).

workspace.description:
The repo and worktree to work in (`{"repo_url", "base_branch", "branch", …}`); absent, a
scratch dir.

NewChain.description:
A chain to write: `[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}` and 1 to 4 entries, at most one of them a
subscription. For an edit this replaces the name and the whole list.

NewChainEntry.description: An entry to write: a pool and the model its accounts run.

model.description: A valid model id; an API-key pool's must be priced. Absent, the harness's default.

pool.description:
The pool's id; it must be the caller's user's, of a `claude`, `codex` or `agy` provider,
and in the chain once.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry safe: the same key on the same issue posts (and wakes) once.

wake_agent_id.description:
The agent to wake (one of the issue's company). Absent: the first agent the body
mentions (`@agent:<id>`, or `@<name>`, any case), else the agent working a `todo` or
`in_progress` issue (its owner), else its next actor. An open question on the issue is
answered by the comment and wakes its asker either way.

color.description: The profile fields (API minor 17) are optional; a field out of shape is a 400.

kind.description: `own` (the default) or `client`; anything else is a 400.

NewConnection.description:

installation. No `Debug`.

email.description: Jira token: the Atlassian account email.

installation_id.description: `app_install`: the GitHub App installation id the setup page returned.

label.description: What people see, 1 to 80 characters; absent, the kind's title.

token.description: The token or API token; written, never read back.

NewConnectionCredential.description: A replacement credential; the same fields as [`NewConnection`]'s. No `Debug`.

ttl_secs.description: Each lease's lifetime; default and most `secrets.lease_secs`.

kind.description:

active at the claim with the `runner` scope, and needs no check code.

name.description: What to call the device that claims it.

scopes.description:
What it may do: within the creator's own scopes. A `runner` invite gets exactly `runner`
(this may be left out).

assignee_agent_id.description: An agent to hand it to at once, which wakes it.

state.description: `backlog` or `todo`; `backlog` when absent, `todo` with an assignee.

runner.description: The runner's device id, `d_…`; it must be in the secret's scope.

kind.description: `device`, `runner`, or `passkey` (a browser, E1-08; only when the Core has passkeys).

name.description: What to call the new device.

scopes.description: What it may do: within the approver's own scopes; a runner gets exactly `runner`.

apply_from.description:

events of this harness and model that have no dollars yet (API minor 18); refused
until the run engine is ported.

input_usd_per_mtok.description: Dollars per million tokens, 0 or more (as `citadel-server price set`).

key.description:
Issue-number prefix, unique in the company: 1-10 capital letters and digits, starting
with a letter (`CIT` for `CIT-12`).

mode.description: Absent: kanban; anything else than `scrum` or `kanban` is a 400.

sprint_approval.description: Who approves a sprint commit; absent: the owner.

team_id.description: The team that owns it, one of the company's.

team_ids.description: Every team, the owner first (API minor 18); wins over `team_id`.

chain.description: An existing chain to put the pool in; default: the user's default chain (made if missing).

pool.description: An existing pool of the provider to join; default: the provider's default pool (made if missing).

project_id.description: The company's project it is for: a hint, named in the CEO's wake.

group.description: The name of a group made with `createSecretGroup`; one level.

runners.description: Active runner device ids; default none.

attach_role.description: The role (matched exactly against an agent's role).

head_agent_id.description: The agent that heads it; absent when it has none.

code.description: The typed code, `ABCDE-FGHJK`: shown once, good once, for 5 minutes.

qr.description: `ainkrad-pair:v1?h=…&p=…&c=<core_fp>&s=<secret>&e=…`, for a QR code: shown once.

is_default.description: The provider's default pool serves an agent bound to none.

A harness and model's price, US dollars per million tokens; each set is a new version, and

seq.description: Its audit sequence number: the cursor of the next page.

Fields to change; absent ones stay. The approval policy and permission mode live on

network_hosts.description: Hosts runs may reach when `network` is not off (API minor 18).

rationale.description: Why the agent proposes it, in one line, when it said.

icon.description: A symbol or emoji (API minor 18); absent when unset, as every field below.

in seconds and how many days worktrees are kept. Stored and shown; not yet applied by

team_ids.description: Every team on it, the owner first; `team_id` is the first.

issues.description: Each done issue, by when it was done.

throughput.description: Top-level issues done in the window.

dropped.description: Sections the budget leaves out of a run's instructions (named there).

injected_bytes.description:
Bytes of the profile a run is given in its instructions, of `budget_bytes` (the
`profile.budget_bytes` setting).

updated_at.description: Absent while the profile was never changed.

mode.description: Scrum to kanban only with no planned or active sprint.

key_prefix.description:

as `sk-or-v1-`). A definition that sets it holds keys, and then only through the gateway
(`delivery` is `["gateway"]`): the broker binds each key to the account's host by it.

models.description:
Model ids exactly as the provider names them: the gateway compares a request's model with
the ids it was granted, as they are, and resolves no alias (`-latest`). `:online` is refused.

priced_at.description: When the models' list prices were read.

test_path.description:
The authenticated path (under the base URL, such as `/key`) of the one-shot account test,
for a provider whose model list needs no key (OpenRouter's is public: a revoked key would
read as `ok`). A user definition without one cannot be tested: the answer is
`inconclusive`. Built-ins use their wire's own model list.

wire.description:
The API dialect the gateway speaks to this provider: `anthropic-messages` (claude),
`openai-responses` (codex) or `gemini-generate` (agy). Optional on write: it is its
harness's own, and any other is refused.

ProviderAccount.description:
An account as a `read` device sees it: its key's last four characters, never the key, the
broker secret's name or the runners it may be leased to.

base_url.description: The provider's base URL when the account was stored.

cap.description: Sessions that may hold the account at once; 0 is no cap.

health.description:
What the scheduler keeps of its health. Only the reads say it; `state`, `state_reason`
and `state_until` (a cooldown's end) are above.

last_test.description: The last one-shot test of the key; absent when it was never tested.

live.description:
Sessions that hold a slot of its cap now (`starting`, `running`, `interrupted`). Only the
reads (`listAccounts`, `getAccount`) say it.

masked_tail.description: The key's last four characters; empty for a key too short to show any.

month_limit_usd_micros.description: The account's monthly dollar budget cap, when one is set; absent when it has none.

month_spend_usd_micros.description:
What the account cost this calendar month (UTC), in millionths of a US dollar, from the
cost ledger. Only the reads say it, and only to an `admin` device.

session_limits.description: What one session may spend through this account; absent when only the budgets limit it.

PushKinds.description: The notification kinds the calling device is pushed (E2-12.3).

kinds.description:
The kinds it opted into, e.g. `approval_needed`; `null` is every kind its scopes allow
(the default). A kind needs its scope on top: a `read` device is never sent an approval.

sandbox.description: A development build's token, for the sandbox gateway.

token.description: The device token, hex, as the app got it from APNs.

Question.description: An agent's question for the admin: a card while open, a receipt once answered.

issue_id.description: The asker's issue, where the answer goes.

raise_tokens.description:
More tokens for the period (millionths of a dollar when the approval's payload `unit`
is `usd_micros`); more than 0.

period_key.description: The period that ran out: `2026-10-22`, a week's Monday, `2026-10` or `total`.

tokens.description: Tokens to add (0 when raising dollars).

usd_micros.description: Millionths of a dollar to add.

RedeemLease.description: A lease to redeem. No `Debug` (review L4).

name.description: 1 to 64 characters, no control characters; trimmed.

ReplaceKey.description: A replacement key, and optionally a new runner scope. No `Debug`.

in_use_by.description:

position.description: Its place in the project's order: the order agents see repos and PRs merge in.

stack.description: What it is built with, "Rust · Node" (API minor 18); empty when unknown.

token_file.description:

anyOf.description: How urgent a request is; `normal` is the `medium` level.

owner_agent_id.description: Who answers in the thread: the CEO, then the product owner it was handed to.

info.description: The Ainkrad Core client API, for the Ainkrad app. Every request is signed by the device's own P-256 key (ES256, raw r||s): the headers Ainkrad-Device, Ainkrad-Session, Ainkrad-Alg (ES256), Ainkrad-Timestamp, Ainkrad-Nonce and Ainkrad-Signature cover an exact canonical string of the Core identity fingerprint, the method, path, query, time, nonce and the body's SHA-256 (handshake spec §5). A session comes from POST /handshake/challenge then POST /handshake/session and lasts 15 minutes; there is no bearer secret, and an Authorization header is refused. A signed body is at most 1 MiB: a larger one is answered 401 auth_failed and counted as a failure against the address, so keep uploads below it. Before trusting a Core, POST /handshake with a fresh nonce and check that core_sig verifies under core_spki and that its fingerprint is the pinned one. Requests carry the server's own Host and no Origin, or the Core's own origin from its web client. A web client signs in with a passkey (POST /handshake/passkey/options, then POST /handshake/passkey/session) and signs every request with a non-extractable WebCrypto P-256 session key in the same way; its event socket takes a one-time ticket (POST /api/v1/ws-ticket) in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol. Times are RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds. Versioning: within /api/v1, enum values, union variants, optional fields and operations may be added; a client must keep an unknown enum value (every enum is open) and skip an event or union variant it cannot decode. Anything removed or renamed is a new /api/v2. `info.version` is `1.<minor>.0`; the minor (`GET /api/v1/me`, `versions.api.minor`) is bumped on every addition.

The run

Its harness finishes the tool call in flight and stops; the run ends `cancelled` once the runner has acknowledged (audited as `run.cancelled`). 409 `run_not_live` when it is over, 502 `runner_failed` when the runner is away (the request is kept)
Its harness is killed now (audited as `run.killed`)
Given to the harness as its next turn (audited as `run.messaged`, its length only). 409 `run_not_live` unless the run is running

The ended run's agent woken again on its issue (audited as `run.retried`); the engine starts it when it is allowed to (budgets, a free runner). A wake already pending for the agent and issue takes it in. 409 while the run is live or for a closed issue
The session's entries with `seq` above `after`, oldest first, at most `limit` (500 by default, 1000 at most), redacted by the platform; an empty transcript for a run with no session yet
The module's tunables with their values, bounds and defaults (`mcp.enabled`, `run.token_ttl_secs`, ...)
Set (audited as `setting.set`); 404 for an unknown name, 400 out of bounds
The deleted sprint: a planned one with no issues whose commit is not waiting on an approval (audited as `sprint.deleted`)
The closed sprint

The sprint, started by the owner (decision #10: the owner the commit gate waits on; audited as `sprint.started`, gate `owner`). A pending commit approval (decide it instead), unpointed issues, an active sprint, or points over capacity without a reason is a 409
Commitment, completion and burndown
The sprint's review and its retro proposals
Every stuck issue, wake or queued run, as of now (read-only: the repair pass acts on the same report while the engine is on)
Deleted; needs a step-up
The team as changed (audited as `team.updated`)
The team as renamed
The team without the agent (audited as `team.member_unseated`); 404 when it had no seat there
The team with the agent seated (or its seat changed; audited as `team.member_seated`); 409 when another agent is the team's product owner or lead; 404 for an agent of another company

202.description: Claimed: the device is pending until the approver matches the SAS; an invite is claimed by its secret alone and the device is active at once (`sas` means nothing then). 401 `pairing_failed` for a wrong, used, expired or burned credential; 400 for keys or proofs that do not hold (the pairing is not spent)

Claimed: a pending device of kind `passkey`, whose key is the credential's public key (the SAS is computed over it); the approver compares the SAS and approves as for any device. 401 `pairing_failed` as for `/pair/claim`; 400 for a credential that does not verify, is not ES256 or comes without options first (the pairing is not spent); 409 for a credential enrolled already

200.description: Registration options for a live pairing of kind `passkey`; nothing is spent, and a new ask replaces the previous ceremony. A wrong, used, expired or burned credential, or a pairing of another kind, is 401 `pairing_failed` and counts as a wrong claim; 400 `passkeys_disabled` when the Core has no passkeys
